name: Tomatoes
description: Fresh locally grown tomatoes are a summer staple at farmers' markets. Varieties range from cherry tomatoes to beefsteak, heirloom, and roma. Rich in lycopene and vitamin C, market tomatoes are far superior in flavour to supermarket varieties.
nutritionHighlights: High in Vitamin C, potassium and lycopene
storageHint: Store at room temperature away from sunlight. Do not refrigerate.

name: Carrots
description: Crisp and sweet locally grown carrots are available across most seasons. Farm-fresh carrots come in classic orange as well as purple, yellow and white varieties. Perfect raw as a snack or roasted as a side dish.
nutritionHighlights: Excellent source of beta-carotene and Vitamin A
storageHint: Refrigerate in a sealed bag for up to 3 weeks.

name: Leafy Greens
description: Spinach, kale, rocket, silverbeet and mixed lettuce are common leafy greens at local farmers' markets. Freshly picked greens retain far more nutrients than packaged supermarket alternatives.
nutritionHighlights: Rich in iron, folate, Vitamins K and C
storageHint: Refrigerate loosely wrapped in damp paper towel.

name: Strawberries
description: Sweet, juicy, locally grown strawberries are one of the most popular items at spring and early summer markets. They are typically sold by the punnet and sell out quickly, so arrive early!
nutritionHighlights: High in Vitamin C and antioxidants
storageHint: Refrigerate and consume within 2-3 days. Do not wash until ready to eat.

name: Mixed Berries
description: Blueberries, raspberries, blackberries and gooseberries are summer gems found at local markets. Locally grown berries are picked at peak ripeness, offering exceptional flavour compared to commercially grown varieties.
nutritionHighlights: Packed with antioxidants, Vitamins C and K
storageHint: Refrigerate immediately. Best eaten within 1-2 days.

name: Corn
description: Sweet summer corn fresh from local farms is a market favourite. Best eaten the same day it is picked, farm corn is far sweeter and more tender than store-bought. Perfect grilled, boiled or used in salads.
nutritionHighlights: Good source of fibre, B vitamins and antioxidants
storageHint: Consume the same day for best sweetness. Refrigerate with husks on.

name: Cucumbers
description: Crisp, refreshing cucumbers are a summer market staple. Available in standard, Lebanese and Persian varieties, fresh market cucumbers have a distinctive crunch and mild flavour that store-bought versions rarely match.
nutritionHighlights: Hydrating, low calorie, good source of Vitamin K
storageHint: Refrigerate for up to one week.

name: Peppers
description: Red, yellow, green and orange capsicums and chilli peppers from local growers are vibrant summer offerings. Freshly picked peppers are sweeter and crunchier, perfect for salads, stir-fries or roasting.
nutritionHighlights: Very high in Vitamin C and antioxidants
storageHint: Refrigerate for up to 1-2 weeks.

name: Pumpkins
description: Autumn brings a wonderful variety of pumpkins and winter squash to farmers' markets. From butternut to jap and kent varieties, locally grown pumpkins are perfect for soups, roasts and seasonal baking.
nutritionHighlights: Rich in Vitamin A, potassium and fibre
storageHint: Store in a cool dry place for up to 3 months.

name: Apples
description: Autumn is apple season at local markets. Expect a dazzling array of heritage and modern apple varieties — Granny Smith, Fuji, Pink Lady, Braeburn and more. Locally grown apples are crunchier and more flavourful than cold-stored commercial varieties.
nutritionHighlights: High in fibre, Vitamin C and antioxidants
storageHint: Store in the refrigerator for up to 6 weeks.

name: Root Vegetables
description: Parsnips, turnips, beetroot, swede and celeriac are the hearty root vegetables that appear as the weather cools. Ideal for soups, stews and roasted dishes, locally grown root vegetables have a depth of flavour that is hard to replicate.
nutritionHighlights: Good source of fibre, folate and Vitamin C
storageHint: Store in a cool, dark place or refrigerate.

name: Citrus
description: Winter is citrus season. Locally sourced oranges, mandarins, lemons, limes and grapefruits bring brightness to the cooler months. Fresh-picked citrus is far juicier and more aromatic than commercially processed alternatives.
nutritionHighlights: Excellent source of Vitamin C and antioxidants
storageHint: Store at room temperature for up to a week or refrigerate for longer.

name: Fresh Herbs
description: Basil, thyme, rosemary, parsley, coriander, chives and mint are commonly found fresh at farmers' markets. Growing your own herbs starts with quality seedlings from market herb vendors.
nutritionHighlights: Rich in antioxidants and anti-inflammatory compounds
storageHint: Store upright in a glass of water at room temperature or wrap in damp paper towel in the fridge.

name: Free-Range Eggs
description: Farm-fresh free-range eggs are a cornerstone of farmers' market shopping. Expect a variety of egg sizes and colours — white, brown and even blue. The yolks of truly free-range eggs are notably richer and more orange than commercial alternatives.
nutritionHighlights: High-quality protein, Vitamins D, B12 and healthy fats
storageHint: Store in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 weeks.

name: Raw Honey
description: Local raw honey is one of the most prized items at farmers' markets. Unprocessed and packed with natural enzymes, local honey reflects the unique flora of the region and varies beautifully between seasons and locations.
nutritionHighlights: Natural antibacterial properties, antioxidants and enzymes
storageHint: Store at room temperature in an airtight container indefinitely.

name: Artisan Bread
description: Sourdough, rye, multigrain, focaccia and specialty loaves from artisan bakers are a highlight of many farmers' markets. Baked fresh the morning of the market, these loaves are a world away from commercially produced bread.
nutritionHighlights: Complex carbohydrates, fibre and B vitamins (especially sourdough)
storageHint: Store in a bread box or paper bag. Slice and freeze for longer storage.

name: Fresh Flowers
description: Seasonal cut flowers and potted plants from local flower growers add colour and joy to farmers' markets. Sunflowers, dahlias, ranunculus, sweet peas and mixed bouquets are common offerings from spring through summer.
nutritionHighlights: N/A — for decoration and gifting
storageHint: Place in fresh water immediately and change water every 2 days.

name: Artisan Dairy
description: Local cheese makers, yogurt producers and small dairies bring a fantastic range of artisan dairy products to market. Soft cheeses, aged cheddar, fresh ricotta and cultured butter are among the highlights.
nutritionHighlights: Excellent source of calcium, protein and fat-soluble vitamins
storageHint: Refrigerate all dairy products. Consume soft cheeses within a week.

name: Radishes
description: Spring radishes are among the first crops to appear at farmers' markets after winter. Crisp and peppery, they add a satisfying crunch to salads and work beautifully with butter and sea salt as a simple snack.
nutritionHighlights: Good source of Vitamin C, folate and fibre
storageHint: Remove tops and refrigerate. Consume within a week.

name: Asparagus
description: Spring asparagus is one of the most eagerly awaited crops of the season. Fresh-picked asparagus should be consumed within a day or two for the best flavour and texture. Look for tight, firm tips and bright green or purple stalks.
nutritionHighlights: Rich in folate, Vitamins K and C
storageHint: Store upright in a little water in the fridge for up to 3 days.

name: Pastured Meat
description: Free-range chicken, grass-fed beef, pasture-raised pork and lamb from local farms are available at select farmers' markets. Ethically raised meat from small local farms offers superior flavour and welfare standards.
nutritionHighlights: High-quality protein, iron, zinc and B12
storageHint: Refrigerate and consume within 2-3 days or freeze immediately.

name: Broccoli
description: Fresh broccoli heads and broccolini from local farms are excellent winter market finds. Look for tight, dark green florets with no yellowing. Farm-fresh broccoli has a noticeably sweeter, nuttier flavour than supermarket broccoli.
nutritionHighlights: Exceptional source of Vitamin C, K and sulforaphane
storageHint: Refrigerate unwashed in a loose bag for up to 5 days.
